investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T02:10:20Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the same error message and zero evidence was collected, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway dependency upstream of the production-api agent provisioning path, not to any individual eval check or its runner logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer propagated this as a 502 bad_gateway on POST /api/agents. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks, none of them could proceed past the initial POST, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api layer and the ELB — consistent with the ~11 s latency before the 502 was returned (failed-check.timing: latencyMs=10997), suggesting a connection timeout rather than an instant rejection.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to be rejected with error code credit_balance_exhausted. The eval failure is scoped to the eval infrastructure's OpenAI credential and does not constitute evidence of a user-facing product outage.
